name: adapter
title: Host adapter
description: The seam between what Gamestage UI renders and what a host performs. It is a TypeScript interface, a React provider and a `useGamestageElement` hook, and it is how a host supplies the things the library refuses to do for itself: analytics, submission, durable storage, settled results, round state, sound and haptics. Every method arrives as a plain function, so the library imports no SDK, opens no socket and calls no fetch. A host that forgets a method gets a compile error rather than a runtime surprise. With no provider at all the built-in adapter runs, keeping state in memory and settling synchronously, so a developer with nothing wired up still gets a game that works and a player cannot tell which implementation is running. Performs nothing: it renders no element, writes no storage and decides no outcome.
docs: Wrap the game in `<GamestageProvider adapter={yourAdapter}>` once, or wrap nothing at all and get the built-in. Inside a component, call `useGamestageElement(elementId)` for `{ player, state, results, settlement, select, commit, report, cue, store }`. Call `commit(optionIds, { optimistic })` with the result you would render anyway: it goes on screen in the same tick as the tap, `settlement` reads `optimistic`, and when the host answers it reads `settled` if the host agrees and `corrected` if it does not. Those are the values `data-gs-settlement` takes, so pass `settlement` straight to `<Stat settlement={...} />`. `submit` returns void and never a promise, because a component that could await a settlement would, and the player would watch a spinner where the feedback should be; the host answers through `subscribeForResults` instead. Components that take an `elementId` prop, such as `choice`, wire themselves up through this hook: give one an id and its selects, commits and settled outcomes travel over the adapter instead of over props. Build a host-backed adapter from scratch, or from `createBuiltinAdapter({ settle })` when only settlement differs.
